hints: Look backwards from the product, 3-oxobutanoic acid has both a ketone at C3 and a carboxylic acid at C1 to build.
Notice that structure 2 already has the 4-carbon acid skeleton, it just needs Cl changed to C=O via an alcohol intermediate.
Check if structures 1 and 3 can also reach that same hydroxy intermediate or be oxidised directly to both carbonyls in only two operations.
walkthrough:
**Meet the target molecule**

Think of 3-oxobutanoic acid as two functional groups to make. It is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COOH}$, a ketone at carbon 3 and a carboxylic acid at carbon 1.

$$\text{target} = \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OH}$$

**Test structure 2, the chloro-acid**

This one is the easiest to spot. It already has the $\text{-COOH}$ group, so only C3 needs changing.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH(aq)}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 / \text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COOH}$$
Step 1 is nucleophilic substitution of Cl by OH. Step 2 is oxidation of a secondary alcohol to a ketone. So 2 works.

**Test structure 3, the bromo-aldehyde**

Here neither carbonyl is correct yet, but both can be fixed cleverly. First hydrolyse the bromide to an alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH(aq)}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$$
Then use strong heated oxidation. This oxidises the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid and the secondary alcohol to a ketone at the same time to give the target. That is still only two steps overall. So 3 works.

**Test structure 1, the unsaturated alcohol**

This is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. First add water across the alkene under acidic conditions to make a diol.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
Then strong heated oxidation oxidises the primary alcohol all the way to $\text{-COOH}$ and the secondary alcohol to a ketone, giving 3-oxobutanoic acid. So 1 works too.
All three routes need only two steps, so 1, 2 and 3 are all possible.

options.A: Correct. All three can give the target in two steps. 2 needs substitution then oxidation, 3 needs substitution then double oxidation, and 1 needs hydration then double oxidation.
options.B: Incorrect. This misses out structure 3. Students often think an aldehyde cannot become an acid while also oxidising an alcohol, but hot acidified dichromate does both in one operation.
options.C: Incorrect. This misses out structure 1. Students often forget that alkenes can be hydrated to alcohols, which can then be oxidised to carbonyls, so the alkene plus alcohol combination is very versatile.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only structure 1 works. It ignores the very straightforward routes from the halogeno-acid and halogeno-aldehyde via NaOH substitution followed by oxidation.
